Senses.Explanation: Literally, cut (斬) kudzu-and-wisteria creepers (葛藤). The parent image names verbal entanglement in Chan records, but this exact compound is very thin and occurs only in late framing prose. One text praises a master for effacing forms and cutting vine-tangle; a preface says that Linji's staff and shout cut all vine-tangle; a biographical preface pairs cutting vine-tangle with destroying thorn thickets. The Zen deviation comes from the established Chan use of creepers for entangling words, here made the object of cutting. Unlike the much commoner longer forms 'cut off the vine-tangle' and 'sever the vine-tangle,' the exact phrase is not attested in this concordance as a live-exchange command, so this entry does not present it as one.
Senses.Note: Exact-form count: 3 hits in 3 allowlisted texts, all curated. One late paratextual sense, mechanically multi-source but narrowly stated. Family checked against vine-tangle (葛藤), cut off the vine-tangle (斬斷葛藤: 16 hits in 15 texts), and sever the vine-tangle (截斷葛藤: 100 hits in 70 texts). Evidence from those longer forms is not assigned to this exact headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 更泯色相，而斬葛藤，於劫火中，振此迦陵。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 萬如禪師語錄, tower inscription for Wanru Tongwei. Gao Shitai is the exact author: the inscription closes with his full signature 高世泰敬讔并書, and the stored verse says Wanru effaced forms and cut entangling vines while raising the kalavinka amid the eon-fire.

Occurrences.Kwic: 達祖單傳，不存知解，滹沱棒喝，盡斬葛藤，縱云一物全無，業已和盤托出。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 笑堂和尚語錄, preface by Chen Zhishen. Chen Zhishen is the exact author: the preface closes with his signature 陳之伸頓首拜撰, and the stored appraisal says the Linji staff and shout cut through all entangling vines.

Occurrences.Kwic: 斬葛藤而誅棘莽，游智刃以無前；抉羅網而破波濤，示慧燈之普照。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 季總徹禪師語錄, preface by Zhang Zhu. Zhang Zhu is the exact author: the section is headed 張銖敘 and closes with his signed colophon, while the stored line says Jizong Che cut entangling vines and thorny growth with the wisdom blade.
